+# Iteration 0.012 · n = 6 of 99 · 2026-09-24 · author: twelve lenses · round 6
+
+## Twelve lenses
+
+### Aset
+SSSES (business case): security 85 · stability 72 · scalability 69 · efficiency 68 · succinctness 66
+
+Founder, investors, customers: I read the deck a sixth time for echoes. The ladder still runs in one order across S1, S2, S11, S15, S16 and S17; the declared model keeps the same words on S3, S8 and S15; the worked event on S4 still reconciles to the ninety minutes S3 prices. This round adds one rule in two places, and I checked that they differ: S16 states the instrument's null and stop rule, S4 applies them to the worked example itself. That is reinforcement with a purpose, each line carrying a fact the other lacks. The register grows to fourteen decisions, and both carriers on S2 and S18 say so.
+
+words: 111
+
+### Asar
+SSSES (business case): security 84 · stability 72 · scalability 70 · efficiency 69 · succinctness 65
+
+Read whole, the deck now says when it would withdraw its own example. Round five gave the founder one event in minutes; round six gives the rule that ends it: if the tabletop's stamped clocks remove fewer than fifteen of the benchmark's one hundred thirty minutes, the example is withdrawn and the model re-derives from what was stamped. For investors, that is the difference between a projection and a hypothesis with a kill condition. For customers, the same rule protects you: no one will defend an assumed minute against your measured one. The synthesis: a business case that can lose is the only kind worth funding, and this one states how.
+
+words: 111
+
+### Athena
+SSSES (business case): security 83 · stability 74 · scalability 71 · efficiency 71 · succinctness 66
+
+Strategy is sequence, and this round the sequence gains its fourth step. S12 now places the public-body pilot after G3 as a numbered entry, not a footnote: one government owner, one project, its people asked through the polling interface. That is the second market appearing in the plan at the point the record can bear it, not before. The stop rule on S4 is strategic too: a founder who pre-commits to withdrawing a number cannot be accused of defending it, and an investor can hold the team to the withdrawal. Founder, the standing risk is unchanged and unnamed: the EDU institution. Every calendar entry after 2026-Q4 waits on that one conversation.
+
+words: 111
+
+### Christo
+SSSES (business case): security 82 · stability 72 · scalability 70 · efficiency 68 · succinctness 66
+
+The citizen stays on the page, and this round the record learns to say no to itself. A null that withdraws an example when the measured minute disagrees is humility written into the method; consensus needs that, because people trust a process that can be wrong out loud. The public-body pilot now has a place in the sequence, after G3, so a community is asked before it is told, and can replay what was decided. Founder, this is how a platform earns the right to carry a crisis for people who never chose it. Investors, trust of that kind compounds. Customers, the rule that protects the founder's number also protects yours.
+
+words: 111
+
+### Enki
+SSSES (business case): security 82 · stability 71 · scalability 68 · efficiency 67 · succinctness 64
+
+Edge cases, again. The stop rule handles the ordinary failure, a small delta; I looked for strange ones. A broken clock: the S16 note now voids the run and records it, never averaging it into a mean that hides it. An approver unreachable beyond succession: the same void. A tabletop that removes more minutes than assumed: the stamped number replaces the assumption in that direction too, which stops the deck from quietly keeping a conservative figure it has beaten. The API shape on S6 assumes every write is an append; the edge is a correction, and the note answers it: a correction is a new version, the old one stays readable.
+
+words: 111
+
+### Enlil
+SSSES (business case): security 85 · stability 75 · scalability 72 · efficiency 72 · succinctness 66
+
+Buildability improved where the innovator asked. S6's note now gives the seven objects an interface shape: every object an addressable, versioned resource with an id, an event, a version, a named writer and a timestamp, read by id or by event, written only by append, exported whole in an open format. A builder can start from that line without inventing conventions. The stop rule on S4 is also buildable: fifteen minutes on a stamped clock is a test a script can run. Founder, what I still cannot build is the first integration, because no buyer has named their stack. Investors, the calendar on S14 holds; nothing this round moved a date.
+
+words: 111
+
+### Krishna
+SSSES (business case): security 84 · stability 73 · scalability 72 · efficiency 69 · succinctness 65
+
+Integration, traced again through the new lines. The interface shape on S6 fixes the contract at the seam: the citizen's answer arrives through the polling interface as an evidence pointer, a partner's fact arrives the same way, and neither becomes the platform's data. The public-body entry on S12 adds no component; it reuses the inbound and the outbound the platform already defines. The null on S16 is measured on the primary clock the platform itself logs, so the instrument and the product share one timestamp source, which is the only way an A/B avoids arguing about whose clock was right. Investors see one architecture; customers see one record; both are unchanged.
+
+words: 111
+
+### Odin
+SSSES (business case): security 83 · stability 72 · scalability 73 · efficiency 68 · succinctness 66
+
+Read this in 2525 and the null still parses: a delta smaller than one-ninth of the benchmark's clock means nothing changed, whatever the tools. That is the foresight this round buys: the deck now carries its own falsification, and a document that can be proven wrong ages better than one that can only be believed. For the founder, the next three years still decide who owns the executive door; a withdrawn example costs a quarter, a defended one costs the company. For investors, the public-body pilot after G3 is the second market appearing in the sequence on its own evidence. For customers, the rule is your protection against a vendor's optimism.
+
+words: 111

+### Pangu
+SSSES (business case): security 81 · stability 71 · scalability 72 · efficiency 68 · succinctness 64
+
+The new thing is still the instrument, and this round it acquires a conscience: a pre-registered null on the primary clock and a stop rule that voids a broken run rather than averaging it away. Few business cases state how they lose before they ask for money; this one does, in a speaker note the founder reads aloud. The interface shape for the seven objects is the second novelty, quiet again: an append-only, versioned record whose export is the whole record, which is what lets a community replay a decision five centuries later. Investors fund an instrument with a kill condition; customers get a vendor who wrote down when to stop.

+### Sofia
+SSSES (business case): security 82 · stability 72 · scalability 69 · efficiency 69 · succinctness 66
+
+Seven readers, one page, a sixth time. The demo audience still gets sentence, loop and ladder from S1. The customer gets the baseline, the quarter, the worked event, and now the rule that would withdraw it. The innovator gets the interface shape on S6, not only data. The investor gets a kill condition on the assumed minute and a fourth sequence entry on S12. The business owner reads a value equation that admits it can fail. The system thinker reads fifteen minutes, not percentages. The execution genius reads a void run recorded, never averaged. The public body reads its own place in the sequence. No reader gets a named institution; honest.
+
+words: 111

+### Thoth
+SSSES (business case): security 86 · stability 75 · scalability 70 · efficiency 71 · succinctness 66
+
+The numbers reconcile, and the new rule is arithmetic on them: one-ninth of the benchmark's one hundred thirty minutes is fourteen point four, rounded to fifteen on the deck, so the null is fewer than fifteen minutes removed. The assumed ninety sits six times above that floor; the rule is a floor for claiming any delta, not a target, and the note says so. Whatever the tabletop stamps replaces the ninety and re-derives the event value, the annual value and the ramp downstream. Void runs are recorded and excluded, so a mean never hides a broken clock. My standing ask holds: one real stamped minute, then let the deck recompute everything.
+
+words: 111

+### Thor
+SSSES (business case): security 88 · stability 74 · scalability 69 · efficiency 68 · succinctness 65
+
+Risk, as the guardian reads it. Last round I asked for a stop rule on the worked example, and S4 carries it: the null, the withdrawal, the re-derivation. That closes the exposure of a number a buyer could quote as a promise; it is now a number the vendor has promised to withdraw. The S16 note adds the void rule for a broken clock or an unreachable approver, the exposure I feared most in a tabletop that becomes evidence. The interface shape on S6 raises one new question: an append-only record with a named writer is discoverable by design, and the privilege-aware fields on S14 remain the answer. Nothing else weakened.
